rationale: All three review lenses ran successfully. The blind lens raised four concerns (migration-path safety, whether the test proves 'retirement', unfixed doc drift, cross-environment config coverage), but the edge-case lens — with full repo access — directly refuted each: no strict component-id enum exists anywhere (Component/ComponentSetting use extra="allow"), the new regression test correctly proves the platform's existing tolerant behavior, the doc-drift note is a deliberate documented plan decision (retiring, not correcting, the doc) rather than an oversight, and repo-wide grep confirms customer-config.yaml is the only file that ever defined aiAdoption (no other config/deploy/CI file references it). The acceptance lens confirmed AC #1 and #2 pass (platform tolerates a lingering aiAdoption entry; no backend surface serves it) and correctly marked AC #3/#4 as deferred per the plan's explicit out-of-scope decision, not as failures. 2 dismissed findings (thin blind-lens concerns fully refuted by edge-case verification); 0 deferred findings.

business_review.criterion: Given a customer configuration file that still enables aiAdoption, when the platform starts, then it starts normally with that entry ignored.
business_review.evidence: config/customer/customer-config.yaml no longer defines the aiAdoption block. New regression test test_load_config_tolerates_retired_ai_adoption_component proves CustomerConfig() loads a YAML still containing an aiAdoption entry without raising (extra="allow", no code dispatches on the id).

business_review.evidence: No DECLARATIONS/CONFIG_IDS entry, no backend endpoint/handler/query references aiAdoption (all removed in EPMCDME-14465). Nothing in this repo can surface adoption content regardless of the flag's presence in a customer config.
